key_insight: Can human forecasters’ written discussions improve cyclone intensity predictions beyond numerical weather data? This study investigates that question across 637 tropical cyclones; the provided abstract is truncated and does not report the results.
problem_solved: Determining whether National Hurricane Center discussions contain useful predictive information not already captured by numerical environmental and wind-field data.
method: Analyze Tropical Cyclone Discussions for 637 Atlantic and eastern North Pacific cyclones from the 2002–2023 hurricane seasons.
Combine discussion text with 13 hurricane environmental predictors from SHIPS and ERA5 10-meter wind fields.
Assess the added predictive value of discussion text beyond the numerical inputs.
impact: The study explores whether expert-written text can complement structured weather data in AI-based forecasting. It addresses a broader ML question: when does human interpretation add information beyond existing numerical inputs?
visual_elements: Two-input diagram: forecaster discussion text and numerical weather data feeding a cyclone intensity prediction.
Atlantic and eastern North Pacific map labeled with 637 cyclones and the 2002–2023 study period.
Comparison schematic: numerical inputs alone versus numerical inputs plus discussion text, without unsupported performance values.
Discussion excerpt illustration alongside icons for environmental conditions and near-surface wind fields.
paper_title: Quantifying the added value of human forecaster discussions for tropical cyclone intensity prediction
paper_authors: Ilia Azizi, Frederick Iat-Hin Tam, Marc-Olivier Boldi, Valérie Chavez-Demoulin, Tom Beucler
